head: 0120c5f643effa9f41f2eb0451843099c31ba78d
summary: I fixed O-019 (M1) in eng/rules-parity.ps1. The must_not_match list loop in Read-Entries now continues past blank lines and comment-only lines (^\s*#). It ends only at a line that is neither blank nor a comment and is indented no deeper than the key; the loop stays bounded by the next entry or the settled marker. So a yaml-only pattern placed after a blank line or a comment is now read and gives DRIFT. Before the fix it gave AGREE: I confirmed that by running the committed (old) reader on the same shape. C-005 in tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 gained four rows, each requiring DRIFT under both powershell.exe and pwsh: a yaml-only pattern after a blank line, after a comment at the key's indent, after a deeper comment, and after a blank line plus a comment. A fifth row is a control: a blank line and a comment between two real items still give AGREE on 21 patterns. The regressions pass: C-001 to C-005, C-007 and the 8 rule Facts.

files.why: O-019/M1: the must_not_match loop continues on blank and comment-only lines, and breaks only on a line that is neither, indented no deeper than the key. Items after a gap are no longer silently skipped.

O-019: four C-005 rows put a yaml-only pattern after a blank line, a comment at the key's indent, a deeper comment, and a blank plus a comment; each must be DRIFT under both shells. A control row checks that a blank and a comment between real items still give AGREE.

obligations.how: Read-Entries now `continue`s on blank and ^\s*# lines and breaks only on a non-blank, non-comment line indented no deeper than the key, with the loop still bounded by $end. C-005 now feeds a yaml-only '(?m)OnlyInYaml' after a blank line, after '    # a note' at the key's indent, after a deeper comment, and after a blank plus a comment. Each exits 1 with 'DRIFT 2 unpaired' and "only in yaml 'OnlyInYaml'" under powershell.exe and pwsh; the control row still gives AGREE. The committed reader gave AGREE (exit 0) on the blank-line shape and the new one gives DRIFT.

Owed to validate-slice, and not changed this attempt. Attempt 1 ran the full harness three times with the same verdict for every row. This fix touches only the parity reader's list loop; the harness runs parity first, and the C-007 clean scenario still passes.
Owed to validate-slice, and unchanged since attempt 1. The harness's two-step rename checks the folder listing shows the new case and not the old before trusting D3/D4/D9 (C-012).
Owed to validate-slice, and unchanged since attempt 1. C-014 flips D13's recorded outcome and the harness exits 1 with DIVERGENCE-CLOSED.

tests.note: All checks held, including the 4 new yaml-only-after-a-gap rows (DRIFT, exit 1) and the control row (AGREE), each under powershell.exe and pwsh.

tests.command: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <temp>/eng/rules-parity-old.ps1 -Root <temp copy with '(?m)OnlyInYaml' after a blank line>
tests.note: Reproduced M1 with the committed reader (git show HEAD:eng/rules-parity.ps1): it printed AGREE, exit 0. The fixed reader printed 'DRIFT 2 unpaired' on the same copy. The temp dir was removed.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1 -Case C-001 (and C-002, C-003, C-004)
tests.note: Regression after the reader change: C-001 8/8, C-002 34/34, C-003 26/26, C-004 26/26, 0 FAIL.
The harness runs parity first; the clean scenario is still CLEAN (17 rules, 7 Facts) and the stray-hit bite still exits 2. 9/9 checks pass.

follow_ups: The yaml reader still refuses (exit 2) some legal YAML shapes rather than reading them, for example flow-style lists and multi-line quoted scalars. That fails closed, which is the design's rule, but anyone hand-editing twinned entries must keep to the header's authoring rules.
